== Enshrined God ==
* {{ill|Izanagi|abstract|Q813858|ar|إزاناغي|az|İzanaqi|bcl|Izanagi|bn|ইজানাগি|bs|Izanagi|ca|Izanagi|cs|Izanagi a Izanami|da|Izanagi|el|Ιζανάγκι|eo|Izanagi|es|Izanagi|fa|ایزاناگی|fi|Izanaki|fr|Izanagi|he|איזאנגי|hr|Izanagi|hu|Izanagi|id|Izanagi|it|Izanagi|ja|イザナギ|ka|იძანაგი|ko|이자나기|lt|Idzanagis|mk|Изанаги|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯒꯤ|no|Izanagi|or|ଇଜାନାଗି|pt|Izanagi|ro|Izanagi|rsk|Изанаґи|ru|Идзанаги|simple|Izanagi|sk|Izanagi|sl|Izanagi|sr|Изанаки|sv|Izanagi|ta|இசநாகி|th|อิซานางิ|tl|Izanagi|tr|İzanagi|uk|Ідзанаґі|vi|Izanagi|zh|伊邪那岐|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagison}} is enshrined as the main deity.
* In addition, {{ill|Kasuga Shrines|ja|春日神社|ko|가스가 신사|zh|春日神社|qid=Q10855011}} (enshrined deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|UNKNOWN|Ame-no-Koyane|lt=Amagiya-no-Mikoto}}) and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takarayu Shrine}} (enshrined deity: {{ill|Kuraokami|de|Kuraokami|it|Kuraokami|ja|淤加美神|sv|Okami-no-Kami|zh|闇淤加美神|qid=Q644201|lt=Takaranokami}}) are also enshrined together.

==Venue==
The area where Taga Shrine is located is also a historically important area, as there are Jomon period ruins such as Tomizawa Ruins and Onoda Ruins, the Onoda Tumulus Group, and {{ill|Sendai Kōriyama Kanga ruins|ja|郡山遺跡|qid=Q11643209}}.

Taga Shrine is ``the oldest shrine in Sendai City,'' and according to the shrine's legend, it was prayed to by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru}} during his conquest of Toi in the 40th year of Emperor Keiko (110). It is said that in the 21st {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|ar|الإمبراطور يورياكو|arz|الامبراطور يورياكو|azb|یوریاکو (ایمپیراتور)|cs|Júrjaku|de|Yūryaku|es|Yūryaku Tennō|fa|امپراتور یوریاکو|fr|Yūryaku|hr|Yūryaku|id|Kaisar Yūryaku|it|Yūryaku|ja|雄略天皇|ka|იურიაკუ|ko|유랴쿠 천황|mr|युराकु|nl|Yuryaku|pl|Yūryaku|pt|Yuryaku|ru|Император Юряку|sh|Car Yūryaku|simple|Emperor Yūryaku|sl|Cesar Jurjaku|sv|Yuryaku|th|จักรพรรดิยูเรียกุ|tl|Emperador Yūryaku|tr|Yūryaku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Юряку|uz|Imperator Yūryaku|vi|Thiên hoàng Yūryaku|yo|Emperor Yūryaku|zh|雄略天皇|zh_min_nan|Yûryaku Thian-hông|zh_yue|雄略天皇|qid=Q357235}} 2nd year ({{ill|458|ab|458|af|458|als|458|am|458 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|458|ar|458|ary|458|ast|458|az|458|azb|۴۵۸ (میلادی)|be|458|be_x_old|458|bg|458|bn|৪৫৮|bpy|মারি ৪৫৮|br|458|bs|458.|ca|458|cdo|458 nièng|ceb|458|ckb|٤٥٨|crh|458|cs|458|cv|458|cy|458|da|458|de|458|el|458|eml|458|eo|458|es|458|et|458|eu|458|fa|۴۵۸ (میلادی)|fi|458|fo|458|fr|458|fy|458|ga|458|gan|458年|gd|458|gl|458|he|458|hi|४५८|ht|458 (almanak jilyen)|hu|458|hy|458|id|458|io|458|is|458|it|458|ja|458年|jv|458|ka|458|kk|458 жыл|ko|458년|la|458|lb|458|lij|458|lmo|458|lt|458 m.|map_bms|458|mdf|458|mg|458|mhr|458|mk|458|mr|इ.स. ४५८|mrj|458 и|ms|458|mzn|۴۵۸|nap|458|nds|458|nds_nl|458|new|सन् ४५८|nl|458|nn|458|no|458|nso|458|oc|458|os|458-æм аз|pa|੪੫੮|pl|458|pnb|458|pt|458|qu|458|ro|458|ru|458 год|rue|458|sa|४५८|scn|458|sd|458ع|sh|458.|shn|458|sk|458|sl|458|sq|458|sr|458|su|458|sv|458|sw|458|tg|Соли 458|th|พ.ศ. 1001|tk|458|tl|458|tly|458|tr|458|tt|458 ел|uk|458|ur|458ء|uz|458|vec|458|vi|458|war|458|wuu|458年|xmf|458|zh|458年|zh_min_nan|458 nî|zh_yue|458年|qid=Q30922}}), he was given 58 bundles of Keida and held a divine ritual ceremony. It is said that in ancient times it was called ``Otakanomiya''.

According to the precinct history book, Taga Shrine was deeply revered by feudal lords and military commanders as the guardian deity of this region. It is said that during the reign of the 70th Emperor Go-Reizei, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|cs|Jošiie Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoshiie|es|Minamoto no Yoshiie|eu|Minamoto no Yoshiie|fa|میناموتو نو یوشی‌ایه|fr|Minamoto no Yoshiie|it|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家|ko|미나모토노 요시이에|pt|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ro|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ru|Минамото-но Ёсииэ|sh|Minamoto no Yoshiie|sv|Minamoto no Yoshiie|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยชิอิเอะ|tr|Minamoto no Yoshiie|uk|Мінамото но Йосіїе|zh|源義家|qid=Q32613}}, the shogun of the military base, crossed the {{ill|Natori River|fa|رود ناتوری|ja|名取川|my|နတိုရိမြစ်|ru|Натори (река)|qid=Q11414763}} and worshiped at the shrine during his eastern expedition, praying for good fortune and long life and dedicating something in his own handwriting.

The temporary shrine built during {{ill|Kyōhō|de|Kyōhō|es|Kyōhō|fa|کیوهو|fr|Ère Kyōhō|ja|享保|ko|교호|ru|Кёхо|simple|Kyōhō|sr|Кјохо|sv|Kyōhō|tr|Kyōhō|zh|享保|qid=Q1145048}} was severely damaged. Afterwards, it was revered by successive lords of the Sendai domain, and the construction of the shrine building was carried out in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga}}4 ({{ill|1775|ab|1775|af|1775|als|1775|am|1775 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1775|ar|1775|ary|1775|arz|1775|ast|1775|avk|1775|az|1775|azb|۱۷۷۵ (میلادی)|ba|1775 йыл|ban|1775|bar|1775|bat_smg|1775|bcl|1775|be|1775|be_x_old|1775|bg|1775|bn|১৭৭৫|bo|༡༧༧༥ལོ།|bpy|মারি ১৭৭৫|br|1775|bs|1775.|ca|1775|cdo|1775 nièng|ce|1775 шо|ceb|1775|ckb|١٧٧٥|co|1775|crh|1775|cs|1775|csb|1775|cv|1775|cy|1775|da|1775|de|1775|diq|1775|el|1775|eml|1775|eo|1775|es|1775|et|1775|eu|1775|fa|۱۷۷۵ (میلادی)|fi|1775|fo|1775|fr|1775|frp|1775|frr|1775|fur|1775|fy|1775|ga|1775|gan|1775年|gcr|1775|gd|1775|gl|1775|gv|1775|he|1775|hi|१७७५|hif|1775|hr|1775.|hsb|1775|ht|1775 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1775|hy|1775|hyw|1775 թուական|ia|1775|id|1775|ilo|1775|io|1775|is|1775|it|1775|ja|1775年|jv|1775|ka|1775|kaa|1775|kk|1775 жыл|kn|೧೭೭೫|ko|1775년|krc|1775 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1775|ku|1775|kv|1775-ӧд во|la|1775|lb|1775|lez|1775 йис|li|1775|lij|1775|lmo|1775|lt|1775 m.|lv|1775. gads|mai|१७७५|map_bms|1775|mdf|1775|mg|1775|mhr|1775|mi|1775|min|1775|mk|1775|mr|इ.स. १७७५|mrj|1775 и|ms|1775|my|၁၇၇၅|myv|1775 ие|mzn|۱۷۷۵|nah|1775|nap|1775|nds|1775|nds_nl|1775|new|सन् १७७५|nl|1775|nn|1775|no|1775|nov|1775|nrm|1775|nso|1775|oc|1775|olo|1775|or|୧୭୭୫|os|1775-æм аз|pa|1775|pl|1775|pnb|1775|pt|1775|qu|1775|ro|1775|ru|1775 год|rue|1775|sa|१७७५|sah|1775|scn|1775|sd|1775ع|se|1775|sh|1775.|shn|1775|simple|1775|sk|1775|sl|1775|smn|1775|sq|1775|sr|1775|su|1775|sv|1775|sw|1775|szl|1775|ta|1775|te|1775|tg|Соли 1775|th|พ.ศ. 2318|tk|1775|tl|1775|tly|1775|tr|1775|tt|1775 ел|ug|1775 - يىلى|uk|1775|ur|1775ء|uz|1775|vec|1775|vi|1775|vls|1775|vo|1775|wa|1775|war|1775|wuu|1775年|xmf|1775|yi|1775|zh|1775年|zh_classical|一七七五年|zh_min_nan|1775 nî|zh_yue|1775年|qid=Q7700}}) with a donation from {{ill|Date Shigemura|fr|Date Shigemura|ja|伊達重村|ko|다테 시게무라|qid=Q846378}}. It is said that the lord of Kakuda Castle, {{ill|Ishikawa Munemitsu|ja|石川宗光|qid=Q11585764}}, presented the shrine with the divine name ``Taga Shrine Izanagison,'' and the shrine was crowded with visitors from his wives and maids.{{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|ceb|Panahon sa Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} It was designated as a village shrine in April 1950, and in 1942 it was enshrined together with Kasuga Shrine in the Onoda district and Horyu Shrine in the Noda district of Higashidai, and in August 1988 it was designated as a Heihaku Kushinsha.

==Precincts==
*Shrine building (haiden, shrine hall, Kasuga-zukuri main hall)
*In addition, there are stone monuments, stone shrines, shrine shrines, sacred {{ill|Quercus dentata|ar|سنديان مسنن|arz|سنديان مسنن|az|Quercus dentata|be|Дуб зубчасты|ca|Quercus dentata|ceb|Quercus dentata|cs|Dub zubatý|de|Japanische Kaiser-Eiche|es|Quercus dentata|fa|بلوط دندانه‌دار|fi|Hammastammi|fr|Quercus dentata|gl|Quercus dentata|hu|Császártölgy|id|Quercus dentata|it|Quercus dentata|ja|カシワ|ka|Quercus dentata|ko|떡갈나무|nl|Japanse keizereik|no|Tanneik|pl|Dąb zębaty|ru|Дуб зубчатый|sv|Quercus dentata|tr|Quercus dentata|uk|Quercus dentata|vi|Quercus dentata|war|Quercus dentata|zh|槲树|zh_min_nan|Ha̍k-chhiū|qid=Q1377319|lt=oak}} trees, a kagura hall, and a shrine office.

==Venue==
It is said that he was solicited by Takeru Takeru of Japan in February 28th year of Emperor Keiko's expedition to the east. It is said that in November of the second year of Emperor Yuryaku's reign (458), a festival was held in which 58 bundles of Keida were offered as a ritual field. To the east of our company, there is a place called ``Keida'', which is named after the ritual field that was given to us at that time.

According to the history of the shrine, when Takeru Takeru of Japan came to Oshu to conquer the east, he suffered from a serious illness due to a series of battles and long journeys. At that time, he set up an altar and a shrine in a warm area where willows grew and prayed for his recovery, and it is said that he recovered and was able to return safely to the land of Yamato. It is said that the shrine where people prayed for recovery from illness and peace of the nation was the origin of Taga Shrine.

The area where our company is located still bears the name of the area associated with this history.
*To the north of Taga Shrine is Kodangahara, the place where Takeru Nihon built an altar to pray for victory in battle.
*``Tanayanagi'' (Tanayanagi → Takayanagi) (current name of the enshrined place) is the place where an altar was made from a willow tree and people prayed for recovery from illness.

Additionally, Shiratori Shrine, which enshrines the spirit of Japan Takeru, is located on the premises of a private house 970 meters southeast of our company.
<gallery widths="200px" heights="150px">
File:Precincts of Shiratori-jinja shrine in Natori city.JPG|Precincts of Shiratori-jinja shrine
File:Shiratori-jinja shrine at Natori city.JPG|Shiratori-jinja shrineFile:Honden of Shiratori-jinja shrine in Natori city.JPG|Honden of Shiratori-jinja shrine
</gallery>

It is said that there have been frequent disputes between our company and Taga Shrine in Tomizawa, Taihaku Ward, Sendai City over which shrine is the Shikinai Shrine, Taka Shrine. The history book ``Shinsen Mutsu Fudoki'' states that ``Taga Shrine was originally located in Tomizawa Village, but is now enshrined in Takayanagi Village.'' However, Taga Shrine in Takayanagi was originally called ``Wakamiya Hachiman,'' but it was renamed Taga Shrine.'' A controversy arose in 1897, which led to the conclusion that Taga Shrine in Tomizawa was Shikinai shrine, and Taga Shrine in Takayanagi was the land where the shrine's territory, such as ritual fields, was located. The place name ``''{{ill|Nishitaga|ja|西多賀村|ko|니시타가촌|qid=Q11627540|lt=Nishitaga}}''' in Taihaku Ward is derived from Taga Shrine in Tomizawa, and the area around our company in Yuriage district and Takayanagi was previously called ``''{{ill|Yuriage|ja|閖上町|ko|유리아게정|qid=Q11655485|lt=Higashitaga}}'''.

It became a local shrine in February 1894, and was later designated as a Heihaku Kushinsha. He was respected by the lord of the domain and the governor of Mutsu Province. In connection with the history of Nihon Takeru, the shrine attracts many worshipers not only from nearby areas but also from other prefectures as a shrine that is particularly blessed with healing from illness and extending life.
